_comment: Cited evidence, not computed output. Every other number in this project is derived from an ABS workbook and validated by the pipeline. These figures are transcribed from a published report and the validation gate does not apply to them, which is why the dashboard renders them in a separate, labelled section.
citation: Taylor, A., Dyrting, S., & Shalley, F. (2020). The Territory and Me Survey: A summary of results. Darwin, NT: Northern Institute, Charles Darwin University.
base: Current Territory residents who had decided whether to stay or leave. Undecided respondents are excluded.
measure: Share intending to still be living in the Territory in two years.

by_birthplace.figure: Figure 6, Two-year Retention Rate by Country of Birth

by_home_ownership.figure: Figure 9, Two-year Retention Rate by Home Ownership
by_home_ownership.note: Only the 18-29 pair is reported here. The report's own text singles out this life stage, and the two values are the ones confirmed numerically rather than read from the bar chart.

precision: Values marked as read from a figure are taken from the published bar charts and are accurate to about a percentage point. 84 and 81 are stated numerically in the report text, as is 76 in the 2020 follow-up summary.
limitations: Stated intentions, not observed behaviour. Nobody followed up to see who actually stayed.
The report publishes no subgroup sample sizes, so the number of people behind each bar is unknown.
Self-selected online sample. The report notes it under-represents people aged 18 to 34 and over 75.
Birthplace and home ownership are each a single-variable split, so the groups overlap and the two findings cannot be separated from each other.
An association with intending to stay is not evidence that home ownership causes retention. The relationship could run either way.
